title: Lobster Rolls
description:
From the Kitchn: Like any dish, lobster rolls are a subjective experience. How do you compare Maine-style
lobster rolls and Connecticut-style lobster rolls? The former consists of a chilled lobster and mayonnaise mixture,
whereas the latter features lobster that’s been warmed in melted butter. Putting these vastly different styles up
against each other felt nearly impossible. “I Tried 8 Popular Lobster Roll Recipes and the Winner Blew Me
Away”: Jasper White’s World Famous Lobster Rolls.
ingredients: 1/3 pound fully cooked lobster meat, or from 3-4, 4-oz lobster tails, freshly steamed (note: it takes about 5 normal whole lobsters to make 1 pound of fully cooked lobster meat)
1+ inches of seedless cucumber, coarsely peeled, finely diced, then slightly salted and drained for a bit
¼ to ½ cup good mayonnaise
dash cayenne pepper or Tabasco sauce (optional, or to taste)
1-2 small scallions (white and some green parts), thinly sliced
2-4 New England-style top-split hot dog buns (or regular hot dog buns, with about 1/4-inch of the sides shaved off to make a flat surface for griddling)
pickles and potato chips, for serving
directions: Place a steamer basket on an upturned colander in the pot so lobster tails are not submerged in the water.
(You might want to use some crumpled-up aluminum foil balls to raise the colander above the water.) Add
some Bay Seasoning or salt for a little extra flavoring.
Pour in water to a depth of 1-2 inches; cover the pot and bring to a boil.
Once the water is boiling, add the lobster tails to the pot and cover.
Steam the lobster tails: 3-6 oz for 4-6 minutes; 6-7 oz for 6-8 minutes; 8-10 oz for 8-10 minutes, etc.
Remove lobster tails from the cooking pot, then plunge in some iced or cold water, to stop cooking.
Cut up the length of the shells and remove the lobster meat. Chop into bite-size, 1/2-inch dice.
Combine the lobster, cucumber, and desired amount of mayonnaise. If the salad is to be served within the
hour, add the scallions. If not, add them 30 minutes before serving. Season with salt if needed and pepper.
Cover with plastic wrap and chill for at least 30 minutes before serving.
When ready to serve, preheat pan over medium low heat. Lightly butter both sides of each bun. Place in
the pan and cook for about 2 minutes or until golden brown. Turn the buns over and toast the other side.
Or toast them under the broiler instead.
When the buns are ready, stuff them with the chilled lobster salad. Place each roll on a plate; garnish with
pickles and potato chips. Serve at once, while the bun is still warm and salad cold.
